text:
Maya: heads-up — multiple clients reported that server-streaming gRPC responses for hosted inference are getting abruptly cut after ~60s when requests go through the cloud LB. Observed as client-side EOF and a short 5xx spike in our router metrics.

jonah: repro steps? which endpoints, any commonalities (region, model size, dedicated vs hosted)?

Maya: happens on hosted (shared) endpoints in us-east-1, mostly long streaming sessions (reasonably large model outputs). Not happening for short responses. Not able to repro locally yet. sample log: `grpc_stream ended: context canceled` on client side.

chao: can you capture a tcpdump next time? my first thought: NAT ephemeral port rotation/timeout or LB sending a FIN/GOAWAY when it decides the backend conn is idle. We saw similar with HTTP/2 windowing before.

Maya: attaching quick tcpdump snippet we grabbed from one backend when a session died:```
12:34:56.789 IP backend->client TCP 443 > 52345: FIN, ACK
12:34:56.789 IP client->backend TCP 52345 > 443: ACK
12:34:56.790 IP backend->client TCP RST
```

sasha: that FIN pattern looks like an intermediate (LB/proxy) tearing down the stream between downstream and upstream then immediately RST. Could be health-check or connection pool eviction. Any correlating logs from the LB? infra-bot, can you grep the LB logs around 12:34:56 for that target?

infra-bot: LB logs: `connection_pool_eviction target=svc-inference-us-east1 reason=idle_timeout age=61s client_conn=active streams=1`

jonah: idle_timeout=61s — aha. That's very close to the symptom. The LB is evicting the backend conn while an active HTTP/2 stream is in flight. That explains the FIN+RST.

chao: root cause hypothesis: cloud LB config has a relatively short backend connection idle timeout (60s). We rely on HTTP/2 stream multiplexing and expect long-lived connections; when the LB evicts the connection it doesn't gracefully terminate active streams (or the proxy in front of backend translates to TCP FIN+RST).

liam: workaround options: 1) bump LB backend connection idle to > streaming TTL, 2) send periodic HTTP/2 pings/keepalives from client or runtime to keep connection active, 3) disable connection reuse on LB (bad perf), 4) move long streams to dedicated capacity route where we control timeouts.

sasha: also need to audit Envoy (edge) settings — older versions had a bug where GOAWAY translation lost half-close semantics and caused immediate RST. Which envoy version are we on in shared pool?

Maya: shared pool envoy: 1.22.3. chao, do we have a quick filter patch to try?

chao: putting a conservative patch that extends idle timeout on the upstream cluster and ensures `gracefulConnectionDraining` is honored. Example snippet we used for local repro: ```yaml
clusters:
  - name: svc-inference
    connect_timeout: 5s
    http2_protocol_options: {}
    common_http_protocol_options:
      idle_timeout: 5m
    drain_timeout: 30s
```

jonah: nice. For immediate mitigation we can 1) change shared LB backend idle to 5m for inference svc only, 2) add a runtime flag to enable periodic HTTP/2 PINGs from our proxy client for streaming sessions >30s, 3) schedule rollout to shared pool after canary.

liam: note cost/perf tradeoff — longer idle on LB means more backend conns held and higher baseline resource use; need to evaluate impact vs moving streams to Dedicated where we already have larger connection pools.

Maya: QA plan: reproduce in staging by lowering keepalive to 30s on a test LB, run a streaming client that emits 1kb frames every 2s, then flip LB to 60s to confirm cut. Chao + jonah will run probe and pcap.

chao: I'll also add an eBPF trace to see if NAT port rotation is also a contributor — earlier incidents showed ephemeral port reuse triggered by cloud NAT which occasionally collides with upstream 5-tuple and causes abrupt resets.

sasha: action items: 
- jonah: change LB backend idle for svc-inference in staging to 5m and run canary (ETA 2h)
- chao: composable envoy patch and eBPF trace (ETA EOD)
- maya: coordinate affected customer comms and collect more client-side logs (ETA 1d)
- liam: perf/cost estimate for longer LB idle vs routing to Dedicated (ETA 2d)

Maya: thanks — please ping here when canary looks good. :thumbsup:

jonah: will do. starting canary now.

infra-bot: canary started for svc-inference in us-east-1, target=10% traffic, ttl=30m.
